transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Laura (Aegis Procurement), Michael (CISO), Ravi (Eng Lead), Emilia (Legal)

Summary: quick procurement / legal kick-off to align on MSA/DPA/SLAs, pricing approval path, and onboarding timeline. Customer has SOC2 and strict data residency needs for PHI-adjacent workloads; primary question around private deployment vs hosted API and SLA levels for 99.9 vs 99.99, plus encryption/KMS and audit log retention. Redwood to provide SOC2, architecture diagram, and redlined contract for customer's legal review.

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making the time. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Laura (Aegis): Laura here from procurement, hi.
[00:12] Michael (Aegis CISO): Michael.
[00:14] Ravi (Aegis Eng): Ravi here.
[00:16] Emilia (Aegis Legal): Emilia, legal counsel.
[00:18] Sofia: Great. Daniel from our SE team is on, he'll handle the architecture and security bits. Daniel, quick hello?
[00:22] Daniel (Redwood SE): Hi all, thanks. I'll jump in on the technical / SLA / deployment questions.
[00:26] Sofia: Goal for today — align on MSA and DPA expectations, SLA targets, give you the materials you asked for, and surface any redlines so we can get procurement moving.

[02:05] Laura: High level — procurement needs to understand pricing approvals; our finance team needs committed capacity numbers and an estimate of unit costs for hosted vs dedicated. Also, timeline — we want vendor onboarded by end of May if possible.
[02:40] Sofia: Understood. We can run a pilot on hosted with a path to Dedicated or Private if you need VPC/on-prem for data residency. Daniel, maybe talk through options and typical latencies/cost deltas?
[03:05] Daniel: Sure. Hosted API gives fastest time to value — simple REST, streaming, and we have per-token pricing. Dedicated reserved pools provide predictable throughput and lower unit cost for sustained load; private deployment (VPC or on-prem) handles strict residency and isolated control plane. Latency: hosted ~20–80ms per token depending on model/seq, dedicated similar but more predictable; on-prem has variable infra-dependent latency. Cost delta: dedicated can be ~30–50% lower per-token for steady usage.
[04:10] Michael: For us, data residency and auditability are the big concerns. Aegis handles PHI-adjacent data; we need encryption at rest and in transit, KMS/HSM integration, and 7 years of audit logs. Can Redwood support that?
[04:40] Daniel: Yes — encryption in transit by TLS, at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments. For hosted we offer envelope encryption options and we can discuss bringing a CMEK for Dedicated in many configurations. Audit logs: we keep request logs and can retain based on plan — longer retention is an add-on we can include. I will send the architecture diagram and exact retention SLAs.
[05:25] Emilia: On the DPA side, we need data processing terms that restrict usage of the data, deletion rights, and right to audit. Also, indemnity language around data breaches needs to be clarified.
[05:40] Sofia: Totally. Our standard DPA restricts model training and any use beyond serving; we can include specific deletion timelines and a SOC2 attestation. For indemnity — we have standard liability caps, but we can surface options in the redline.

[07:00] Laura: Procurement will need an MSA with clear termination rights and SLAs tied to credits for downtime. Our legal will push for 99.99 for some endpoints.
[07:20] Daniel: Can you describe which endpoints you plan to put behind the highest SLA — is it low-latency chat, batch embedding, etc? That helps define the right SLA tiers.
[07:40] Ravi: Primary workloads: patient triage assistant (chat, low-latency) and a nightly batch embed job. The triage assistant needs high availability and low p99 latency. Batch can tolerate higher latency.
[08:00] Michael: So we probably want 99.95 or 99.99 for the triage endpoint. Pricing impact?
[08:12] Sofia: Higher SLA (99.99) often implies reserved capacity / Dedicated with failover across zones and an SLA credit matrix. We'll include those options in the pricing sheet.

[09:30] Emilia: Also, SSO / SAML integration for RBAC — we need SCIM provisioning and role-based access controls for the console and APIs.
[09:45] Daniel: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning in the Console, plus RBAC. For Private deployments we can tie into your IdP directly.
[10:12] Michael: Audit trail again — token-level logs, per-route logging, and exportability to our SIEM for 7 years. Is exporting logs supported to S3 or a log collector?
[10:30] Daniel: We can stream logs to your S3 or to a log collector via TLS; for hosted we have integrations with Splunk/Datadog. I'll document the retention and export options.

[12:00] Sofia: On pricing approvals — what's your procurement gating? Are you looking for a standard PO, or do you need contingent on legal signoff?
[12:12] Laura: Procurement moves fastest with commercial terms and fixed pricing. However legal signoff is required before PO is issued. Target approvals: procurement sign-off mid-April, legal takes a week after redline review, then finance PO. End of May onboarding seems achievable if legal gets MSA by next week.
[12:40] Sofia: Great — we'll prioritize the redline. I'll send our standard MSA and DPA with suggested edits for the indemnity and SLAs.

[14:10] Michael: A technical question — KV cache and prefix caching — we need to ensure the model doesn't store persistent patient identifiers in cache beyond request boundaries. How is caching handled?
[14:30] Daniel: Good callout. Our runtime uses ephemeral KV cache per session; we have policies to drop sensitive tokens on commit/rollback. For Dedicated and Private you can configure longer or shorter cache times; we can also disable prefix caching for sensitive endpoints. I'll include implementation notes; apologies if docs call it "K V cache" in places, we sometimes see OCR typos in earlier docs.
[15:20] Laura: On DPA — we need a clause for subprocessor disclosure and a 30-day notification for changes.
[15:30] Emilia: Also, we require breach notification within 72 hours and assistance with regulatory notifications.
[15:40] Sofia: Our DPA includes subprocessor lists and change notifications; 72-hour breach notification is aligned with our standard practice, but I'll confirm exact wording with legal.

[17:00] Ravi: From an engineering perspective, we'd run an initial pilot on hosted to validate prompts and regressions, then scale to Dedicated. How long is a typical pilot and what telemetry do you provide for evals?
[17:20] Daniel: Pilots typically run 2–4 weeks. We provide token-level cost metrics, per-route latency and throughput, and quality metrics if you provide eval prompt sets. We also support canary rollouts and model pinning so you can A/B test model variants.
[18:05] Laura: Pricing — can you provide committed capacity discounts and an example invoice? CFO wants line items: base monthly, committed GPU hours, overages, support tier.
[18:25] Sofia: Yes — we'll include committed capacity tiers, burst pricing, and optional premium support for SLA-backed response times. I'll include an example invoice and a three-tier committed example.

[20:00] Emilia: Indemnity — we'll propose removing certain liability caps for gross negligence or willful misconduct and push on data breach carveouts.
[20:18] Sofia: Understood. We have standard caps but we can escalate to legal for carveouts; I'll flag that in the redline and set up a legal-to-legal call.

[22:00] Michael: For compliance, can you share your SOC2 report and ISO certs? Also, pen test schedule?
[22:12] Daniel: Yes — SOC2 Type II report available; ISO in progress. We do annual pen tests and can share summary reports and remediation notes under NDA. I'll attach SOC2 and the pen test summary in the notes I send.

[24:00] Laura: On onboarding timing — if legal gets redline back by 4/16 and they review quickly, PO by 4/28, can we have onboarding in the first week of May?
[24:12] Sofia: That's feasible. We have onboarding templates and a dedicated CSM for enterprise. We'll confirm availability.

[26:00] Daniel: One more technical: KMS integration — for Hosted we support envelope encryption; for Dedicated/Private you can bring your own KMS with rotation policies. Key rotation and key access logs are supported.
[26:25] Michael: Good. We want proof of no model training on customer data — explicit in DPA.
[26:40] Sofia: We'll make that explicit: no training on customer data, no retention beyond configured retention windows, and ability to delete customer data on request.

[29:00] Emilia: Can you send your standard DPA and highlight the clauses around training, deletion, breach, and subprocessors?
[29:10] Sofia: Yes — will do.

[31:00] Laura: Any competitor issues — our security team asked whether you use any third-party model providers.
[31:10] Daniel: We host curated open models and have verified performance profiles; we also run in-house runtime. If you require, we can commit to specific model binaries and versions.

[33:00] Sofia: Recap / next steps: Daniel will share SOC2, architecture diagram, KMS details; I'll send redlined MSA/DPA and pricing with committed tiers; schedule legal-to-legal call week of 4/20. Customer to confirm procurement timelines and any required redline priorities.

[35:00] Emilia: We'll prioritize indemnity, data residency, and breach notif. Laura will confirm procurement path.

[37:00] Ravi: Technical follow-ups — can you include a sample deploy recipe for Dedicated and an estimate of time to spin up reserved pool?
[37:12] Daniel: Yes — typical time to provision Dedicated reserved pool is 2–4 weeks depending on capacity, but we can often provision faster if it's a standard GPU profile. I'll include a deploy recipe.

[40:00] Sofia: Any final Qs?
[40:10] Michael: No, thanks. Just want to see the SOC2 and full audit log options.
[40:20] Sofia: We'll send those tonight/tomorrow.

[42:00] Emilia: Thanks, we'll review and get back with redlines.

[42:10] Sofia: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials and schedule the legal call.

[42:20] Laura: Thanks all.

[42:25] Sofia: Bye.

Action items (captured above): Sofia to send MSA/DPA + pricing; Daniel to send SOC2, arch diagram, KMS details; customer legal to provide redlines.

References / shared artifacts: "Redwood MSA v3.pdf" (sent), "Redwood DPA standard - 2026.pdf" (to be sent), SOC2 Type II report (to be sent), Pricing sheet (to be sent).
